terms: Vite-native test runner — Jest jaisa API, par bahut fast aur ESM/TS out of the box.
Har test se pehle chalne wali file (matchers extend, MSW start).
t0_0.what: Definition: Vitest vite.config.ts ke test block se configure hota hai. Component tests ke liye environment: 'jsdom', globals: true (describe/it global), aur setupFiles mein jest-dom matchers import hote hain.
t0_0.why: Vite ka same transform pipeline use hota hai, isliye alias, TS, JSX alag config ke bina chalte hain. Watch mode HMR jaisa instant feedback deta hai.
pros: Fast, same Vite config, TS/ESM native
cons: Kuch Jest-specific plugins/mocks ka behaviour alag
gotchas: globals: true ke saath TS types (vitest/globals) add karo
Default environment node hai — DOM tests ke liye jsdom set karo
CI mein vitest run (watch nahi)

terms: Table-driven tests: ek test, kai input/output rows.
t0_1.what: Definition: describe tests ko group karta hai, it/test ek case hai, expect(value).matcher() assertion hai. test.each se ek hi logic ko kai data par chalate hain.
t0_1.why: Tests documentation bhi hain: naam aisa rakho ki fail hone par pata chale kya toota. Table-driven tests duplication hata dete hain.
cons: Over-specified tests refactor ke time break hote hain
gotchas: Objects par toBe fail hota hai — toEqual/toStrictEqual
Ek test mein ek behaviour check karo
Snapshot sparingly — bade snapshots koi review nahi karta

terms: Mock function jo calls record karta hai.
Existing method ko wrap karke track/override karta hai.
Poore module ko replace karta hai (hoist hota hai).
t0_2.what: Definition: Mocks dependencies (API, timers, modules) ko fake karte hain taaki test fast aur deterministic rahe. mockReturnValue, mockResolvedValue, mockImplementation se behaviour set hota hai; vi.clearAllMocks()/restoreAllMocks() se reset.
t0_2.why: Unit test ko network/DB par depend nahi hona chahiye. Lekin zyada mocking implementation se chipak jati hai — boundaries (network, time) par mock karo, apne internal functions par nahi.
cons: Over-mocking tests ko brittle banata hai
gotchas: vi.mock file top par hoist hota hai — upar ke variables use karne ke liye vi.hoisted
Mocks tests ke beech reset karo
Network ke liye MSW module-mock se behtar

t0_3.what: Definition: Async tests mein async/await use karo aur hamesha await/return karo, warna test pehle hi pass ho jata hai. Time-based code ke liye fake timers: advanceTimersByTime(ms).
t0_3.why: Real setTimeout par sleep karne se tests slow aur flaky hote hain. Fake timers debounce/polling logic ko milliseconds mein test kar dete hain.
cons: Fake timers + promises ka interaction tricky (async variants chahiye)
gotchas: Await bhool gaye to test bina assert ke pass ho jata hai
Fake timers ke baad useRealTimers restore karo
Promises ke saath advanceTimersByTimeAsync use karo

terms: Kaun si lines/branches tests ne chalayin.
v8: native, fast; istanbul: instrumentation, zyada accurate branches.
Minimum coverage jo CI mein enforce hota hai.
t0_4.what:
Definition: vitest run --coverage report banata hai (lines, branches, functions). Coverage ye batata hai kya chala, ye nahi ki kya sahi check hua.

Config, types, trivial getters aur generated code ko exclude karo; critical logic par branch coverage dekho.
t0_4.why: 100% coverage ka target gaming aur bekaar tests laata hai. Behtar: critical paths par high coverage + threshold taaki girne na paaye.
cons: Coverage quality guarantee nahi hai
gotchas: Executed != asserted: bina assert wale test bhi coverage dete hain
Coverage ko target mat banao, signal samjho
Branch coverage line coverage se zyada useful hai

terms: Har test independent chale — shared mutable state nahi.
Temporarily skip, sirf ye chalao, ya pending marker.
t0_5.what: Definition: Lifecycle hooks (beforeAll, beforeEach, afterEach, afterAll) setup/teardown handle karte hain. Nested describe mein hooks scope ke hisaab se chalte hain. test.todo planned tests ka marker hai.
t0_5.why: Test order par depend karne wale tests flaky aur debug karne mein mushkil hote hain. Har test apna data khud banaye aur cleanup kare.
cons: Heavy beforeAll shared state isolation tod sakta hai
gotchas: it.only commit na ho — CI mein poori suite skip ho jati hai
Shared module-level variables tests ke beech leak hote hain
Hooks ke andar async await karo

terms: User ko jo dikhta/hota hai test karo, state/internal function nahi.
Test jitna real use jaisa, utna confidence.
Implementation badle par test na tute.
t1_0.what: Definition: RTL ka motto: 'The more your tests resemble the way your software is used, the more confidence they give you.' Component ko render karo, user ki tarah interact karo (click, type), aur screen par jo dikhta hai wo assert karo.
t1_0.why: Implementation tests (state variable ka naam, instance method) refactor par toot jate hain bhale hi app sahi chale. Behaviour tests sirf tab todte hain jab user-facing cheez badle.
cons: Real browser behaviours (layout) jsdom mein nahi
gotchas: Component ke internal state/hooks ko test mat karo
Snapshot par over-depend mat raho
Layout/CSS checks ke liye E2E/visual tests chahiye

terms: Sabse preferred query — accessible role + name se.
getBy: turant ya error; queryBy: null return; findBy: async wait.
Last resort jab koi semantic query na mile.
t1_1.why: Role-based query accessibility ko saath-saath validate karta hai: agar getByRole('button', {name}) mil gaya to screen reader user ko bhi milega.
cons: Role/name samajhne ka learning curve
gotchas: getBy multiple match par error deta hai — getAllBy use karo
Absence ke liye getBy nahi, queryBy
testid sirf last resort

terms: Real user interactions simulate: focus, pointer, keyboard events ka poora sequence.
Sirf ek low-level DOM event dispatch karta hai.
Instance banao, phir await karke use karo (v14).
t1_2.what: Definition: @testing-library/user-event click par hover → mousedown → focus → mouseup → click jaisi poori sequence chalata hai, type par har key ka keydown/keyup. fireEvent.click sirf ek click event deta hai.
t1_2.why: Real browser jaisa behavior test hota hai (jaise disabled button par click kuch nahi karta). Isliye user-event default hona chahiye.
cons: fireEvent se thoda slow aur async
gotchas: v14 mein userEvent.setup() pehle karo aur await karo
fireEvent sirf jab user-event support na kare (jaise kuch custom events)
Fake timers ke saath advanceTimers option do

terms: getBy + waitFor: element aane tak wait.
Callback ko tab tak retry jab tak pass na ho ya timeout.
React ko state updates flush karne deta hai; RTL zyada tar khud wrap karta hai.
t1_3.what: Definition: Async UI (API ke baad data dikhna) ke liye await screen.findByText() use karo. waitFor assertion ko retry karta hai; waitForElementToBeRemoved loading spinner ke hatne ka wait karta hai.
t1_3.why: Fixed sleep (setTimeout) slow aur flaky hota hai. Polling-based waits tab tak chalte hain jab tak condition true na ho, aur jaldi khatam hote hain.
cons: Timeout default 1s — slow cases mein badhao
gotchas: waitFor ke andar side effects (click) mat karo
Ek waitFor mein ek hi assertion rakho
'not wrapped in act' warning aksar await missing hone ka signal hai

terms: Providers (Router, QueryClient, Theme) ke saath render wrapper.
Router/hooks ko vi.mock se replace karna.
Sirf network/browser APIs mock karo, apne child components nahi.
t1_4.what: Definition: Component ko context chahiye (Router, React Query, Redux) to ek renderWithProviders helper banao jo wrapper deta hai. Child components ko mock sirf tab karo jab wo bahut heavy ya third-party ho (chart, map).
t1_4.why: Har test mein providers repeat karna noisy hai. Zyada mocking (apne hi child components) tests ko integration se door aur brittle bana deta hai.
cons: Over-mocking se confidence kam
gotchas: Har test ka naya QueryClient banao (cache leak se bachne ke liye)
Query retry false karo tests mein
Apne child components ko mock mat karo

terms: Automation sirf ~30–40% a11y issues pakadta hai.
t1_5.what: Definition: axe(container) rendered DOM par WCAG rules chalata hai (missing labels, bad contrast, invalid ARIA). Role-based RTL queries bhi accessibility ka implicit test hain.
t1_5.why: Regression pakadne ka sasta tareeka hai. Lekin keyboard flow aur screen-reader experience manually ya E2E (Playwright + axe) se verify karni padti hai.
cons: jsdom mein color contrast aur layout rules nahi chalte
gotchas: Passing axe ka matlab fully accessible nahi
Contrast checks real browser (Playwright) mein
Keyboard navigation ke tests alag likhne padte hain

terms: Mock Service Worker — network level par requests intercept karta hai.
Node (Vitest/Jest) ke liye; setupWorker browser ke liye.
listen() before all, resetHandlers() after each, close() after all.
t2_0.what: Definition: MSW real network layer par requests ko intercept karta hai, isliye fetch/axios/React Query code ko pata bhi nahi chalta ki mock hai. Node mein setupServer(...handlers), browser mein service worker.
t2_0.why: Module-level mocks (vi.mock('axios')) code ke tareeke se chipak jate hain. MSW ke saath wahi code chalta hai jo production mein — sirf response fake hota hai.
where: backend ready na ho to browser worker.
cons: Initial setup aur handlers maintain karna
gotchas: onUnhandledRequest: 'error' se unmocked calls turant dikhti hain
Server ko shared setup file mein start karo
Node 18+ mein global fetch ke saath msw v2 use karo

terms: Ek route ka mock: method + path + resolver.
t2_1.what: Definition: Handlers http.get/post/put/delete(url, resolver) se banate hain. Resolver request padh sakta hai (await request.json(), query params) aur HttpResponse return karta hai.
t2_1.why: Ek handler set realistic backend jaisa behave kare (validation, 404) to tests aur dev dono mein kaam aata hai.
cons: Handlers backend se drift kar sakte hain
gotchas: Relative URLs ke liye base URL environment mein set ho
Request body ek baar hi read hota hai — clone karo
Order matter karta hai: pehla matching handler jeetta hai

terms: Latency simulate: loading states test karne ke liye.
t2_2.what: Definition: Sirf happy path nahi, error aur loading states bhi test karo: 4xx/5xx responses, network failure, slow response (await delay(500)) aur empty list.
t2_2.why: Production bugs aksar error/empty/loading states mein hote hain jo manually test nahi hote. MSW se in sab ko deterministic bana sakte ho.
t2_2.code:
import { http, HttpResponse, delay } from 'msw';

http.get('/api/items', () => HttpResponse.json([]));                       // empty
http.get('/api/items', () => HttpResponse.json({ message: 'boom' }, { status: 500 })); // server error
http.get('/api/items', () => HttpResponse.error());                        // network failure
http.get('/api/items', async () => { await delay(1500); return HttpResponse.json(items); }); // slow
cons: Bahut scenarios test suite ko lamba bana sakte hain
gotchas: Retry logic wale clients (React Query) tests mein retries off karo
delay('infinite') loading state hamesha dikhata hai
Error format backend jaisa rakho

terms: Ek test ke liye handler override.
Har test ke baad defaults wapas.
Handler sirf pehli request par chale.
t2_3.what: Definition: Default handlers happy path dete hain; kisi ek test mein alag response chahiye to server.use(http.get(...)) se override karo. afterEach(() => server.resetHandlers()) overrides saaf karta hai.
t2_3.why: Har scenario ke liye alag handlers file nahi banani padti. Override sirf us test tak rehta hai, isliye isolation bani rehti hai.
cons: resetHandlers bhool gaye to leaks
gotchas: resetHandlers afterEach mein zaroor
Overrides defaults se pehle match hote hain
Parallel tests ek hi server share karte hain — files isolated rakho

terms: Operation name se match karte hain.
Specific endpoint URL ke liye scoped handlers.
t2_4.what: Definition: GraphQL sab kuch ek endpoint par POST karta hai, isliye MSW URL ki jagah operation name se match karta hai: graphql.query('GetUser', ...).
t2_4.why: Apollo/urql/React Query jaise clients ko bina badle test kar sakte ho. Variables inspect karke conditional responses de sakte ho.
cons: Operation ka naam hona zaroori (anonymous queries match nahi hoti)
gotchas: GraphQL errors 200 status ke saath aate hain, HTTP error nahi
Query ko naam do (anonymous mat rakho)
Partial data + errors dono ho sakte hain

terms: Ek handlers.ts jo tests, Playwright aur dev mode teeno use karein.
Browser mein MSW start karke backend ke bina UI develop.
t2_5.what: Definition: src/mocks/handlers.ts ko Vitest (setupServer), browser dev (setupWorker) aur Playwright (page.route ya MSW) mein reuse karo. Data builders/factories bhi share hoti hain.
t2_5.why: API contract badle to ek jagah update karna hota hai. Frontend backend ke bina develop kar sakta hai aur tests wahi data dekhte hain jo dev mein dikhta hai.
cons: Handlers ko real API ke saath sync rakhna padta hai (contract tests help)
gotchas: Mock data prod bundle mein na jaye (dynamic import + env guard)
Service worker file public folder mein chahiye (msw init)
Handlers drift ko contract tests se pakdo

terms: Projects (browsers), baseURL, retries, workers, reporters ka config.
chromium / firefox / webkit / mobile viewports par same tests.
Test se pehle dev/preview server start karna.
t3_0.what: Definition: Playwright config mein projects alag browsers/devices, use.baseURL, retries (CI par 1–2), workers (parallelism) aur reporter (html/github) set hote hain. webServer app ko khud start karta hai.
t3_0.why: Cross-browser coverage (khaas kar WebKit/Safari) E2E ka bada fayda hai. Trace on-first-retry se failures debug karna aasan hota hai.
cons: Browsers download aur CI time
gotchas: CI par npx playwright install --with-deps chahiye
Retries flakiness chhupate hain — trace dekh kar fix karo
Parallel tests ke liye data isolate rakho

terms: Playwright action se pehle actionability (visible, enabled, stable) khud check karta hai.
Locator multiple elements match kare to error — ambiguity pakadta hai.
t3_1.what: Definition: Locators user-facing queries se banao: getByRole, getByLabel, getByText, getByTestId. Chain/filter: page.getByRole('listitem').filter({ hasText: 'Asha' }).
t3_1.why: CSS/XPath selectors UI refactor par toot jate hain. Role-based locators stable bhi hain aur accessibility ko bhi encourage karte hain. Manual waitForTimeout ki zarurat nahi.
cons: Ambiguous locators strict mode error dete hain (accha signal)
gotchas: waitForTimeout avoid karo — web-first assertions (expect(...).toBeVisible())
CSS class selectors fragile hain
locator.count() par assertion retry nahi karta — toHaveCount use karo

terms: Page ki interactions ko class mein wrap karna.
Selectors aur flows ek jagah — UI badle to ek file update.
Page object ko test mein inject karne ka Playwright tareeka.
t3_2.what: Definition: POM mein har page/component ke liye class banti hai jo locators aur actions (login(email, pw)) expose karti hai. Tests business language mein likhe jate hain, selectors tests mein nahi.
t3_2.why: Bade suites mein selectors duplicate hote hain; UI change par 30 tests todte hain. POM se maintenance sasta hota hai. Chhote suites mein overkill ho sakta hai.
cons: Extra abstraction; chhote projects mein overkill
gotchas: Page objects mein assertions kam rakho (tests mein assert)
Bahut deep inheritance (BasePage chains) avoid karo
Component-level objects (Modal, Table) bhi banao

terms: Test ke liye setup jo automatically banta/cleanup hota hai (test.extend).
Poori run se pehle ek baar chalta hai.
t3_3.what: Definition: Har test mein UI se login karna slow hai. Ek setup project login karke storageState file save karta hai; baaki tests use: { storageState } se authenticated shuru hote hain. Fixtures worker-scoped ya test-scoped ho sakte hain.
t3_3.why: E2E suite ka bada hissa auth aur data setup mein jata hai. Fixtures aur saved state se tests tezi se aur isolated chalte hain.
cons: Shared state file expire/rotate hone par dhyaan
gotchas: .auth folder git mein commit mat karo
Tests ke beech shared mutable data se flakiness
Fixture mein cleanup (await use(x) ke baad) zaroor karo

terms: Page/element ka baseline image se pixel compare.
t3_4.what: Definition: Pehli run baseline snapshot banati hai; baad ki runs compare karti hain. UI intentional change par --update-snapshots. Dynamic content ko mask ya animations ko animations: 'disabled' karo.
t3_4.why: CSS regressions (spacing, overflow, wrong color) jo functional tests nahi pakadte, visual tests pakadte hain. Lekin OS/font differences se noisy hota hai — CI (Linux, docker) mein hi baselines banao.
cons: Noisy aur baselines maintain karna padta hai
gotchas: Local macOS aur CI Linux ke baselines alag honge
Animations aur lazy images se flaky diffs
Har cheez ka screenshot mat lo — sirf high-value screens

terms: Mock: fake response; seed: real backend mein data API se banana.
t3_5.what: Definition: page.route('**/api/items', route => route.fulfill({ json })) se network layer mock hota hai. Real backend ke saath E2E ke liye test data API se seed karo (request fixture).
t3_5.why: Third-party/flaky/rare cases (500 error, slow response) ko deterministic banane ke liye mock; aur core happy path ke liye real backend, taaki contract bhi test ho.
cons: Over-mocking E2E ke real-ness ko kam karta hai
gotchas: Route page.goto se pehle register karo
Glob patterns precisely match karo
Bahut mocking = E2E ka fayda ghat jata hai

terms: Fail hone wala test, minimum code se pass, phir clean up.
London: mocks, outside-in; Detroit (classicist): real objects, inside-out.
Design ko test ke through shape karna.
t4_0.what: Definition: TDD loop: pehle ek failing test (red), phir sabse simple code jo usse pass kare (green), phir refactor. Pure logic aur bug fixes (pehle repro test) mein sabse zyada kaam aata hai; UI/exploratory kaam mein overhead lag sakta hai.
t4_0.why: Chhote steps, fast feedback aur testable design milte hain. Lekin dogma banake har line pe lagu karna productivity gira sakta hai — judgment chahiye.
cons: Exploratory / UI-heavy kaam mein slow lag sakta hai
gotchas: Implementation ke around tests likhoge to refactor mushkil
Tests ko public behaviour par rakho
Mock-heavy London style design couple kar sakta hai

terms: Bahut unit, kam integration, bahut kam E2E.
Kent C. Dodds: static + unit + integration (sabse zyada) + E2E.
Anti-pattern: zyada E2E/manual, kam unit — slow aur flaky.
t4_1.what: Definition: Test types ka mix: static checks (TypeScript, ESLint), unit (pure logic), integration (components + hooks + network mock), E2E (real browser). Frontend mein integration tests aksar best ROI dete hain.
t4_1.why: Unit tests fast par kam confidence; E2E zyada confidence par slow/flaky. Cost-confidence balance sahi rakhna hi testing architecture hai.
cons: Layer boundaries team mein debate ka vishay
gotchas: Sab kuch E2E se cover karne ki koshish mat karo
Coverage % ko goal mat banao
Flaky E2E ko quarantine karo, ignore nahi

terms: Tests ko kai machines/jobs par baantna.
node_modules/Playwright browsers cache se install time bachana.
Sasti checks (lint/typecheck) pehle, mehengi baad mein.
t4_2.what: Definition: GitHub Actions workflow: checkout → actions/setup-node with cache → install → lint/typecheck → unit tests → build → E2E (sharded). Branch protection mein required checks set hote hain, test report artifact upload hota hai.
t4_2.why: Slow CI developers ko block karti hai aur log tests ignore karne lagte hain. Caching, parallel jobs aur fail-fast se feedback minutes mein milta hai.
t4_2.code:
name: CI
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  checks:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version: 22, cache: npm }
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm run lint && npm run typecheck
      - run: npm run test:run -- --coverage
  e2e:
    needs: checks
    strategy: { matrix: { shard: [1, 2, 3] } }
    steps:
      - run: npx playwright install --with-deps
      - run: npx playwright test --shard=${{ matrix.shard }}/3
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        if: failure()
        with: { name: pw-report-${{ matrix.shard }}, path: playwright-report }
cons: CI cost aur maintenance
gotchas: Cache key lockfile hash par rakho
Failure par traces/reports artifact upload karo
Secrets forks ke PR mein available nahi hote

terms: Frontend (consumer) batata hai API se kya expect karta hai.
Contract testing tool: consumer test se pact file, provider verify karta hai.
Contract tootne par provider build fail.
t4_3.what: Definition: Consumer test mock provider ke against chalta hai aur ek pact (JSON contract) banata hai. Backend CI mein wahi pact real provider par replay hota hai; mismatch = breaking change pakda gaya, deploy se pehle.
t4_3.why: E2E ke bina bhi 'backend ne field rename kar diya aur frontend toot gaya' jaise bugs rokta hai. Microservices/multiple teams mein sabse useful.
pros: Breaking API changes jaldi pakde jate hain
cons: Setup + team agreement + broker infra
gotchas: Contract sirf utna specify karo jitna consumer use karta hai
Provider states maintain karne padte hain
Chhoti single-team app mein overkill ho sakta hai

terms: JS bundle size ko CI mein assert karna.
t4_4.what: Definition: Performance ko test suite ka hissa banao: size-limit bundle budget, Lighthouse CI thresholds, aur Playwright mein PerformanceObserver se LCP/CLS read karke assert.
t4_4.why: Performance regressions silent hote hain; automated checks unhe PR stage par pakadte hain, production ke baad nahi.
cons: Lab numbers noisy — thresholds par buffer rakho
gotchas: CI machines variable hote hain — multiple runs / relaxed thresholds
Production RUM ke saath complement karo
Realistic throttling set karo

terms: Bina code change ke kabhi pass kabhi fail.
Flaky test ko main gate se hata kar alag track karna.
Same input = same result: fixed time, seed, isolated data.
t4_5.what: Definition: Flakiness ke aam kaaran: timing/race conditions, shared state, real network, random data, animation, test order dependence. Fix: auto-waiting/web-first assertions, isolated data, fake time, mocked network, aur retry sirf diagnosis ke liye.
t4_5.why: Flaky tests trust tod dete hain — team failures ignore karne lagti hai. Quarantine + tracking + root-cause fix ek process hona chahiye.
cons: Root-cause hunting time leti hai
gotchas: Retries flakiness chhupate hain — rate track karo
Test order par depend mat raho
Real time/random/network ko control mein lao
